Estimate HRF shapes from other runs, with optional spatial regularization

Source: R/crossrun_hrf.R
estimate_crossrun_hrf.Rd

Estimate HRF shapes from other runs, with optional spatial regularization

Usage

estimate_crossrun_hrf(
  bold,
  events,
  tr,
  kernel_grid,
  nuisance = NULL,
  valid_rows = NULL,
  time_offset = 0,
  spatial_groups = NULL,
  pooling = c("voxel", "parcel"),
  spatial_strength = 0,
  fallback_kernel = 1L,
  min_r2 = 0.01,
  min_training_runs = 1L,
  min_parcel_voxels = 5L,
  batch_size = 2048L,
  return_scores = FALSE,
  amplitude_model = c("condition", "trial"),
  noise_model = c("ar1", "ols"),
  noise_rho = NULL,
  noise_grid = seq(-0.8, 0.9, by = 0.1),
  evidence = c("calibrated", "legacy"),
  evidence_alpha = 0.05,
  canonical_strength = 0.01,
  spatial_coords = NULL,
  spatial_fwhm = NULL,
  selection_mode = c("hard", "soft_average"),
  noise_groups = NULL
)

Arguments

bold

Named list of time-by-voxel numeric matrices for one participant. Voxel column IDs must be unique and identical in all runs, in the same order.

events

Named list of data.frames with onset (seconds), condition, and optional duration (seconds, default zero). Names/order must match bold.

tr

Common acquisition interval in seconds. All runs use the same grid.

kernel_grid

Matrix or list of equal-length candidate causal HRFs, sampled at tr starting at lag zero. Use hrf_library() or supply explicit candidates.

nuisance

Optional matching list of time-by-regressor matrices. An intercept and linear trend are always included separately for each run.

valid_rows

Optional matching list of logical observation masks; FALSE and NA omit rows from training fits without deleting their acquisition times.

time_offset

First acquisition time, scalar or named numeric run vector.

spatial_groups

Optional voxel parcel labels, named in voxel column order. Labels must be nonmissing and nonempty. Parcels must be defined independently of target-run responses; no implicit whole-brain parcel is constructed.

pooling

Select HRFs per voxel or share one HRF per supplied parcel.

spatial_strength

Nonnegative fixed penalty on voxel candidate distance from the training-derived parcel HRF; requires spatial_groups. Zero disables the soft penalty. Only used with voxel pooling; not automatically tuned.

fallback_kernel

Index of the prespecified fallback candidate, default 1.

min_r2

Minimum mean adjusted partial R-squared for a supported selection, default 0.01. This is a configurable heuristic, not a significance threshold.

min_training_runs

Minimum usable other runs per voxel, default 1.

min_parcel_voxels

Minimum eligible training voxels per parcel, default 5.

batch_size

Maximum voxel columns per native scoring block.

return_scores

Retain candidate-by-voxel training score matrices per fold.

amplitude_model

Training amplitudes shared within condition (fast default), or free for each event record (trial). Trial amplitudes can support HRF estimation when signed trial responses average to zero, but cost more and require a design with sufficient residual degrees of freedom.

noise_model

Default ar1 uses pooled, grid-REML covariance estimates; ols disables whitening. Pooling uses supplied spatial_groups or the run.

noise_rho

Optional fixed AR(1) coefficient, scalar or named in run order. Bypasses noise estimation. Requires noise_model = "ar1".

noise_grid

Ordered AR(1) grid within [-0.95, 0.95], default -0.8 to 0.9 in steps of 0.1. Boundary estimates are explicitly labeled.

evidence

Default calibrated uses conditional GLS F tests with library corrections, prespecified-shape comparison, and training-run compatibility. Legacy retains the adjusted-R-squared heuristic. Conditional tests are exact for known Gaussian AR covariance and a correct mean model; estimated noise, non-Gaussian errors, and model misspecification require empirical validation.

evidence_alpha

Per-voxel evidence threshold, default 0.05. Corrects the candidate search and compatibility comparisons across training runs, not multiple testing across the brain. Not a posterior probability.

canonical_strength

Fixed shape-distance penalty toward fallback_kernel in calibrated mode, default 0.01. Zero removes this additional shrinkage.

spatial_coords

Optional numeric matrix of 3D voxel coordinates (N x 3) used for local Gaussian-weighted anchor pooling.

spatial_fwhm

Optional numeric spatial Gaussian FWHM (in coordinate units) for local anchor pooling.

selection_mode

Candidate selection rule: `"hard"` (default) selects a single discrete winning HRF column index per voxel/parcel; `"soft_average"` constructs a continuous Empirical-Bayes / Boltzmann evidence-weighted composite HRF kernel across compatible neighborhood candidates blended with the prespecified fallback kernel.

noise_groups

Optional voxel labels defining noise covariance pooling neighborhoods, in voxel column order. Defaults to spatial_groups when omitted. Allows noise neighborhoods (e.g., tissue- or sub-parcel-informed groups) to differ from HRF selection parcels.

Value

An object of class crossrun_hrf with normalized kernels, per-target-run selections and training manifests, parcel anchors, run status/design summaries, optional candidate scores, voxel/run IDs, and frozen settings. When `selection_mode = "soft_average"`, also includes per-target-run candidate weight matrices (`kernel_weights`) and unit-sum composite HRF kernel matrices (`selected_kernels`).

Details

When multiple runs are supplied, each target run is excluded from its own HRF selection, including parcel anchors and fallback decisions. When only a single run is supplied (`length(bold) == 1L`), usable observations are partitioned into contiguous temporal sub-blocks (3 blocks for longer runs, 2 halves for shorter runs) that are scored against the full causal event design using full-run AR(1) covariance estimates and pooled across sub-blocks with cross-block compatibility testing, while returning a single-run `crossrun_hrf` object for full-run deconvolution. Training fits have run-specific condition or event amplitudes and nuisance coefficients, with one shared candidate HRF across conditions. They do not fit unrestricted trial timecourses or use RPE. Native SVD projections are shared across voxel blocks. Scores are adjusted partial R-squared after removing nuisance, averaged equally across usable training runs. Parcel scores average these voxel scores equally, retaining voxel-specific amplitudes rather than averaging BOLD first. In voxel mode, selection maximizes score minus spatial_strength times normalized squared distance to the reliable parcel anchor. Weak/insufficient voxel fits fall back to a reliable parcel anchor, then the prespecified fallback kernel. This is a discrete shape penalty, not Bayesian posterior inference, a local adjacency prior, or spatial smoothing of neural activity. Library, thresholds, parcels, and penalty must be fixed externally or tuned within training data. Calibrated mode additionally penalizes distance from the prespecified shape. The legacy gate accepted null free-event fits in colored-noise simulations. Calibrated mode tests task support, departures from the prespecified shape using pairwise encompassing models, and compatibility with every usable training run. Fisher combination uses independent runs; Bonferroni corrections account for candidate comparisons. Unsupported or inconsistent shapes fall back. Parcel anchors are admitted either when at least min_parcel_voxels voxels are individually supported or when the parcel-level Cauchy-combined p-value (hrf_cauchy_p(), valid under arbitrary spatial correlation within a parcel) passes the candidate-corrected evidence threshold. Run compatibility cannot be assessed with a single training run. There is no access to target-run vascular shape or guarantee of transfer to that run. AR covariance is estimated per run using a fixed event-amplitude mean model and, when residual degrees of freedom allow, its first two temporal derivatives. Noise likelihood profiles are pooled, not the BOLD signals. All whitening uses the original acquisition clock, including gaps. No automatic nested tuning or physiological amplitude calibration is included. Nonfinite/constant/nuisance-only voxel runs are omitted; observation masks are common across voxels. Candidate task ranks must match within a run and leave residual degrees of freedom, otherwise that run cannot inform HRF selection.
